subject: Model fit playbook + TPS/latency profiles for Kindred pilot

Subject: Model fit playbook + TPS/latency profiles for Kindred pilot

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the materials we committed to share:

1) Discovery highlights (short):
- Primary workload: clinical note summarization + patient Q&A (single-turn, structured output)
- Expected median request size: ~120 tokens; 95th percentile ~420 tokens
- Target SLA: p95 latency <= 350 ms for interactive UI; throughput target for pilot ~120 TPS burst / 40 sustained
- Data residency: US-only, pre-processing in customer infra, no PHI to Redwood-hosted logs without agreement

2) Initial model fit recommendations (high level):
- Candidate A: redwood-7b-q4 (fastest, good quality for summarization; recommended for UI-tier to meet latency SLO)
- Candidate B: redwood-13b-int8 (stronger on long-form coherence; higher TPS cost but better quality on complex notes)
- Fallback: redwood-7b-int8 quantized variant for capacity-constrained regions

3) Perf profiles and what we measured: attached is a Redwood-verified performance pack (redwood_verified_perf_profiles_kindred_q2.pdf). Key numbers from our lab runs (baseline HW: A100-80GB-equivalent):
- redwood-7b-q4 @ batch=1: p50=45ms, p95=120ms, sustained TPS=95
- redwood-7b-q4 @ microbatching: sustained TPS=220 (with 40ms added latency p95)
- redwood-13b-int8 @ batch=1: p50=110ms, p95=300ms, sustained TPS=40

Notes: these are measurements on our curated prompt set (see kindred_prompt_pack_v1.zip). Your real-world numbers may vary; we recommend running a 48h lightweight pilot to validate token distribution and prefix-cache hit rates.

4) Immediate next steps (I can take point):
- Share prompt pack + perf pack (attached) — actioned
- Proposed pilot scope: 2-week pilot, 3 endpoints (UI low-latency, batch inference for daily digest, hybrid fallback) — see pilot_scope_mop.md
- Hand off to engineering for trial capacity estimate (Karthik will follow up with recommended Dedicated vs Hosted config by EOD Thursday)
- Procurement intro for SOW and non-disclosure (cc'd)

If anything above is off, tell me now — otherwise I'll schedule the kickoff for next Tues and Karthik will send the perf/cost tradeoff note.

Best,
Hannah

Thanks Hannah — this is super helpful. A couple quick clarifying questions from the eng team: 

- For the redwood-7b-q4 numbers, are the p95s measured with prefix caching enabled or cold-starts? We expect high repetition across our corpus which should help but want to size correctly.
- You listed sustained TPS=220 with microbatching — is that per GPU instance or per model shard? What's the recommended instance spec if we want to hit ~120 TPS sustained with p95 <350ms?

Also: we're sensitive to any small regressions in quality when we move to q4/int8 variants. Can you point to a minimal regression guardrail (prompt tests / evals) you'd recommend we run during the pilot?

Appreciate it — Sarah
Sarah Li

Subject: Re: Model fit playbook + TPS/latency profiles for Kindred pilot

+1 to Hannah's recap — quick clarifications from perf side.

- p95 context: the redwood-7b-q4 p95=120ms in the attached PDF is for warm runs with prefix/KV cache enabled (typical chat-like cache hit rate ~60% in our prompt pack). Cold-start p95s can spike ~2.5x for longer sequences.
- The sustained TPS=220 figure is for a single optimized serving instance with multi-streaming + microbatching (our runtime will coalesce up to ~32 concurrent streams before batching kicks in). Practically, for your target ~120 TPS sustained with headroom we recommend: 1 x g5.48-like (8 GPU) Dedicated pool with autoscale=1..3 and instance-level concurrency tuned to 16-24. That gives you ~2.5x headroom for bursts and keeps p95 around target.

Quality/regression guardrails we recommend for the pilot:
- Baseline eval set (we included 120 prompts in kindred_prompt_pack_v1.zip) covering common summarization cases + 20 adversarial prompts for hallucination checks
- Monitor: rouge-l, exact-match for structured slots, and a simple heuristic for hallucination (presence of unsupported dates/IDs)
- Thresholds: require no more than 3% absolute drop in rouge-l and <1% hallucination rate increase when moving 13b->7b-q4 for critical flows

I'll attach a one-page checklist in the Drive folder (uploaded). If you want, we can run an automated regression job that compares redwood-13b-int8 against 7b-q4 on your prompt set overnight.

—Marissa

Principal Applied ML, Redwood Inference
